children: Tencent (TCEHY), China's gaming, social-media and digital-services heavyweight, rose to $56.19 Wednesdayeven as demand for Enflame's initial public offering went through the roof. The Tencent-backed chipmaker's online tranche was subscribed a staggering 6,109 times, turning the listing into a stampede for Chinese AI exposure.

More than seven million accounts chased the shares. Only 0.025% secured an allocationroughly one winner for every 4,000 applications. Enflame is raising 6.1 billion yuan, or approximately $908 million, to develop fifth- and sixth-generation AI processors. That capital could accelerate its technology roadmap, but the unprofitable chipmaker still must prove it can convert hype into sustainable earnings.

Tencent's second-quarter results showed revenue rising 11% to 204.8 billion yuan, while attributable profit increased less than 1% to 56 billion yuan. At $56.19, the stock trades 18.55% below its $68.99 GF Value estimate, pointing to a meaningful valuation gap. Enflame gives Tencent another route into China's domestic AI-chip push, but eye-popping IPO demand is only the opening actprofitable execution is what ultimately matters.

title: Tencent Rose as Its AI Chip Bet Draws 6,109 Times Demand
